_meta.indication: LATUDA is indicated for the treatment of patients with schizophrenia.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, 6-week US study comparing lurasidone 40 and 120 mg/day vs placebo (1:1:1).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acute exacerbations of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in BPRS total score at week 6
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean BPRS change from baseline: -3.8 (placebo), -9.4 (40 mg; p=0.018), -11.0 (120 mg; p=0.004); both doses superior to placebo.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, 6-week US study comparing a single lurasidone dose of 80 mg/day vs placebo (1:1).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acute exacerbations of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in BPRS total score at week 6
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean BPRS change from baseline: -4.2 (placebo) and -8.9 (80 mg; p=0.0118); 80 mg superior to placebo.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, 6-week, placebo- and active-controlled, fixed-dose trial of lurasidone 40 and 120 mg/day with an olanzapine 15 mg/day active control; US and non-US sites.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acute exacerbations of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in PANSS total score at week 6 (MMRM)
pivotal_trials.result: Placebo-adjusted LS mean PANSS change from baseline: lurasidone 40 mg -9.7, lurasidone 120 mg -7.5, olanzapine 15 mg -12.6 (all adjusted p<0.05 except olanzapine).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, 6-week, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose trial of lurasidone 40, 80 and 120 mg/day vs placebo; US and non-US sites.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acute exacerbations of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in PANSS total score at week 6 (MMRM)
pivotal_trials.result: Placebo-adjusted LS mean PANSS change from baseline: lurasidone 40 mg -2.1 (p=0.591), 80 mg -6.4 (p=0.011), 120 mg -3.5 (p=0.391); only 80 mg superior to placebo.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5% and at least twice placebo) were somnolence, akathisia, nausea, parkinsonism and agitation. Somnolence was reported in 22.3% (224/1004) of LATUDA vs 9.9% (45/455) placebo; akathisia incidence was 15.0% vs 3.3% placebo; nausea 12% vs 6% placebo. Akathisia and somnolence were dose-related.
target_moa: Atypical antipsychotic; efficacy thought to be mediated through combined central dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptor antagonism; lurasidone is a high-affinity antagonist at D2 (Ki=0.994 nM), 5-HT2A (Ki=0.47 nM) and 5-HT7 (Ki=0.495 nM) and a partial agonist at 5-HT1A.

boxed_warning.content: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs; LATUDA is not approved for treatment of patients with dementia-related psychosis.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the drug is not the first in its class and the safety profile is similar to other approved drugs for this indication.

description.text: Added 120 mg strength tablet and increased maximum dosing for schizophrenia patients to 160 mg/day

citations.quote: These "Prior Approval" supplemental new drug applications propose adding the 120 mg strength tablet and increasing maximum dosing of patients with schizophrenia to 160 mg/day (S-005) and changes to carton and container labels of professional samples (S-007).

description.text: Added treatment of bipolar I depression as monotherapy and as adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate

citations.quote: These “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug applications propose the following additional indications: treatment of patients with depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder (bipolar depression) as monotherapy and as adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate.

description.text: Added treatment of schizophrenia in adolescents (pediatric patients ages 13-17 years)

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications propose the addition of safety and efficacy data for the treatment of schizophrenia in adolescents (S-026) and the addition of safety data in pediatric patients for irritability associated with autistic disorder (S-027).

description.text: Added indication for treatment of children and adolescents with major depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder as monotherapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes the indication of treatment of children and adolescents with major depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder as monotherapy.

summary.text: Standard NDA under section 505(b) for an atypical antipsychotic; the application was based on four short-term trials, approved October 28, 2010 for schizophrenia in adults, with deferred pediatric studies required under PREA and two additional postmarketing commitments; no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received December 30, 2009, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Latuda (lurasidone hydrochloride) 40 mg and 80 mg tablets.
This application is based on data from 4 short-term trials.

Your application for lurasidone was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class and the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for this indication.

requirement.text: 1701-1: Deferred pediatric study under PREA — study to obtain pharmacokinetic data and dosing information for lurasidone in schizophrenia patients ages 13 to 17 years.

citations.quote: 1701-1 A deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of schizophrenia in pediatric patients ages 13 to 17 years. A study to obtain pharmacokinetic data and provide information pertinent to dosing of lurasidone tablets in the relevant pediatric population.

requirement.text: 1701-2: Deferred pediatric study under PREA — study of the efficacy and safety of lurasidone tablets in schizophrenia patients ages 13 to 17 years.

citations.quote: 1701-2 A deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of schizophrenia in pediatric patients ages 13 to 17 years. A study of the efficacy and safety of lurasidone tablets in the relevant pediatric population.

requirement.text: 1701-3: Evaluate the longer-term (maintenance) efficacy of lurasidone in adults with schizophrenia using a placebo-controlled, randomized-withdrawal design with open-label stabilization prior to double-blind randomization.

citations.quote: 1701-3 To evaluate the longer-term, i.e. maintenance, efficacy of lurasidone in the treatment of adults with schizophrenia. This trial must be placebo-controlled, utilize a randomized withdrawal design, and include an adequate period of stabilization with open-label treatment of lurasidone prior to double-blind randomization.

requirement.text: 1701-4: Further characterize use of lurasidone in adults with schizophrenia at a dose lower than 40 mg (e.g., 20 mg daily) through an adequate and well-controlled trial.

citations.quote: 1701-4 It is not apparent from the trials you have conducted in schizophrenia that the lowest effective dose of lurasidone has been identified. We ask that you further characterize the utilization of lurasidone in the treatment of adults with schizophrenia with a dose lower than 40 mg (e.g. 20 mg daily) through an adequate and well controlled trial.
